t:
(a) In General.—Section 8062 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(h)(1) Beginning October 1, 2011, the Secretary of the Air Force may not retire more than six B–1 aircraft.“(2) The Secretary shall maintain in a common capability configuration not less than 36 B–1 aircraft as combat-coded aircraft.“(3) In this subsection, the term ‘combat-coded aircraft’ means aircraft assigned to meet the primary aircraft authorization to a unit for the performance of its wartime mission.”. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 132 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1320) is amended by striking subsection (c).

fable.w: The section only limits how many B-1 aircraft the Secretary of the Air Force may retire, requires a minimum number of combat-coded aircraft, and makes a conforming amendment. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given any role, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. There is no tempting contrary reading; it is purely an internal force-structure directive.

opus.w: The section limits how many B-1 aircraft the Secretary of the Air Force may retire and requires keeping at least 36 combat-coded aircraft. It provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The only actor is a federal official, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. A military decision being regulated is not the same as outsiders taking part in that decision.
opus.s: Beginning October 1, 2011, the Secretary of the Air Force may not retire more than six B–1 aircraft.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a numerical limit on the retirement of military aircraft by the Secretary of the Air Force. It does not require consultation with, or participation from, any entities outside the federal government. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the Department of Defense.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Air Force may not retire more than six B–1 aircraft
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "combat-coded aircraft" implies a decision-making process involving military units or external stakeholders, but the text strictly limits the action to the Secretary of the Air Force's internal management of assets. There is no mention of consulting with states, the public, or other outside entities. The decision is purely internal to the Department of Defense.
